understood: Subscribers can pause a subscription instead of cancelling it.
While paused, billing stops and the customer keeps their account and history.
The subscription resumes later and billing starts again.
Not yet clear: who can pause, for how long, and what a paused customer can still use.

items.label: Choose how long to pause
items.detail: Pick a length or a resume date
items.example: Pause for 1 month, 2 months, 3 months, or until a date I choose.

items.label: Resume billing
items.example: On the resume date Atlas charges the card and sends a receipt.

items.label: Reminder email
items.example: Your subscription resumes in 3 days and your card will be charged.

says: The customer opens Manage subscription and sees Pause next to Cancel.
They choose how long to pause, and confirm.
Atlas marks the subscription Paused and stops invoices and charges.
When the pause ends, billing starts again and the card is charged.
A reminder email goes out shortly before that, if you want one.
Pause length, access while paused and the reminder are not decided yet.

questions.question: How long can a customer pause for?
questions.why: Without a limit, paused subscriptions could sit forever. A fixed list is simpler to build than any date, and I would otherwise guess.
options: Any date up to 3 months away
Any length, until they resume it
The business owner sets the limit

questions.question: While paused, what can the customer still do or use?
questions.why: This decides whether a pause is a break from paying only, or also a break from the service. It also affects what the business owner expects.
options: Keep full access, just stop paying
Read-only access to past invoices and data

questions.question: How does billing start again?
questions.why: Automatic resume is easy but can surprise people with a charge. Manual resume needs follow-up and may mean lost revenue.
options: Only when the customer resumes it

questions.question: Should we email the customer before the pause ends?
questions.why: A reminder cuts down on complaints and refunds, but it is an extra email to design, send and test.

questions.question: Who can pause: the customer on their own, or only the business owner for them?
questions.why: Self-service means a new screen for the customer. Owner-only means a new action in the owner's dashboard, and your request says customers.
options: Customer, and the owner can also do it
